chapter: From Pittsburgh to Maxine Sullivan: management and style
title: The Kirby and Frankie Newton band shuffle at the Onyx
summary: She discusses the 'giant fight' and how the Onyx band changed after she arrived.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Absolutely. Do you remember any of the circumstances which led to the - I read somewhere where it was described as the 'giant fight' between Kirby and Frankie Newton, when he was replaced by . . .

I wasn't aware of it but I do know that when I went into the Onyx Club in the beginning that Frankie Newton was in the group and I learned one way or the other that it was Frankie Newton's band. They didn't have these guys like Charlie Shavers and Russell Procope. In fact, Pete Brown was on alto sax.
It was much more of a junk band than the highly organized disciplined group.

That's right, a different group altogether. I don't know how Kirby did it but I did know that when Russell Procope and Billy Kyle, Charlie Shavers and O'Neil Spencer came in off the road, they had been on the road with Lucky Millinder, and the next thing I knew they were a brand new band there. And Frankie Newton was not on the scene anymore. I wasn't aware of the, of any conflict there between the two of them but

all I know is . . . MR. HUGHES: Leadership? I don't think it was that so much. I think that Kurby probably had his own ideas about what he wanted to do and persuaded Joe Helback to let him do it. And that's Frankie Newton on trumpet, on my recording of 'Loch Lomond' and also Pete Brown. I don't know just what Kurby did unless he decided that he was going to, instead of just having, as you said a little junk band, he was going to do something else and he needed the right kind of guys to do it with.
I think Frankie Newton got to play with other groups and the next thing I knew, he wasn't there anymore.
